children: The White House launched "Trump TV," a 24/7 YouTube livestream, on Monday. The move comes days after President Trump banned journalists from CNN, Politico, and MS NOW over their coverage of his administration.
The inaugural video was a stream of Trump speaking at Mount Rushmore on July 3 as part of a livestream titled “Trump TV: The Essentials Station.” The stream started at 7 p.m.
“Watch the Trump Administration’s biggest moments all in one place,” read the stream’s description on Google's
YouTube. “Top videos, major remarks, and must-see highlights streaming 24/7 and updated in real time. Stay informed and stay up to date!”
The White House used a similar description on the social platform X but added that “Not every big moment has made it on your TV, now it can.”

pool coverage of the White House in solidarity with a

) have suspended coverage and issued a joint statement reminding the administration that “the public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”
Gavin Newsom calls move 'autocratic'
California Gov. Gavin Newsom slammed Trump TV’s rollout in the wake of the ban.

“First, Trump banned independent news from the White House,” Newsom wrote on X. “Now, he’s launching what is quite literally state-run TV to try drowning out the fact that he and his corrupt administration are failing the American people. This is truly autocratic behavior from a failed President.”
